text:
olga: quick flag — security-ci found a Vault-transit ciphertext blob committed in a vendor onboarding repo. It references projects/redwood-infra/locations/us/keyRings/onboard/cryptoKeys/relay-wrap. No plaintext in the commit.
sam: link?
olga: https://github.com/vendor/example-app/commit/abc1234 (vendor sent us the repo copy). The blob string looks like `vault:v1:...` and wraps a transit key that appears to be backed by our KMS key.
marta: if the transit key is wrapped with our KMS key, the ciphertext in the git history could allow decrypt iff attacker also has access to KMS Decrypt. We need to triage KMS IAM bindings + Vault wrapping config.
lee: agree. immediate plan: 1) snapshot KMS IAM policy; 2) check KMS Audit logs for Decrypt/AsymmetricSign in last 90d; 3) identify which Vault cluster/mount created the cipher; 4) ask vendor to remove commit and force-push history rewrite; 5) rotate wrapping key and transit key if needed.
sec-bot: INCIDENT-2026-045 created: sec-545123 (severity: medium). Assigned: eng-security.
oncall: pinging vault oncall for potential rewrap issues @oncall.
oncall: I can be available for the rewrap; need maintenance window if rewrapping transit master key.
olga: initial findings: KMS policy for that cryptoKey includes two bindings: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter for serviceAccount:relay@redwood-prod and also roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter for group:external-integrations@vendor. That's bad — vendor group should not have direct Decrypt.
sam: how did that binding get in place? probably from an earlier onboarding script that added the group to the key to allow vendor to run dev harness.
marta: remove vendor group binding immediately (but check for active uses). I'll prepare an IAM delta that revokes vendor group, adds a conditional binding allowing decryption only from `resource.name.startsWith("projects/redwood-prod/")` and specific serviceAccounts.
lee: before revoking, let's audit logs for any Decrypt by vendor principals: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type=kms_crypto_key AND protoPayload.methodName:google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:external-integrations@vendor' --limit 1000`
olga: ran that query — zero Decrypts from vendor group in last 180d. The commit may be stale.
vendor-eng: we found the sample while triaging internal onboarding repo. We can remove the commit and rebase history now; we'll also rotate anything in our CI that pulled the blob. We can provide a signed attestation of removal.
marta: good. Still proceed with least-privilege changes and enable a log-based alert. I'll draft the IAM patch:
```
- remove: members: group:external-integrations@vendor
- add: condition: allow only serviceAccount:relay@redwood-prod or roles bound to infra CI
```
sam: vault questions: if we rotate/rekey the KMS key that's wrapping Vault transit master key, do we need to rewrap existing ciphertexts? Vault supports rewrap of the wrapping key but if the ciphertext is transit-wrapped it should be fine. Need to confirm Vault's `wrap_access` and `transit/wrapping_key` settings.
marta: correct, but safest is to: 1) snapshot `vault read sys/mounts/transit`, 2) backup transit keys `vault read -format=json transit/keys | jq .`, 3) run `vault rewrap` if configured. We'll coordinate in staging first.
lee: create an audit metric: log-based metric `kms_decrypt_external` where protoPayload.methodName contains "Decrypt" and principalEmail !startsWith "relay@redwood-prod" -> trigger pagerduty.
marta: also enable VPC-SC or organizational constraints for that key ring to reduce cross-project access.
oncall: rewrap/rotation maintenance window: we can do staged rewrap this evening 19:00-20:00 PT with a rolling approach. I suggest staging at 19:00, prod at 19:30.
sec-bot: attached runbook: https://confluence.redwood/security/incident-runbooks#git-commit-secrets-kms-ciphertext
olga: vendor pushed a PR that removes the blob and history rewrite is in progress. Vendor will also rotate any local artifacts.
vendor-eng: confirmation: we will force-push corrected history in 15m and provide a signed deletion manifest (sha256 for removed blob and commit id).
sam: ops checklist I'm running:
- snapshot KMS key IAM: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy relay-wrap --location=us --keyring=onboard --project=redwood-infra > relay-wrap-iam.json`
- snapshot KMS audit logs: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type=kms_crypto_key' --limit 2000 > kms-audit.json`
- snapshot Vault mount config: `vault read sys/mounts/transit`
- list transit keys: `vault list transit/keys`
- grep for vault ciphertext patterns in repo mirrors: `git grep -n "^vault:v[0-9]:" || true`
marta: RBAC change PR: https://git.redwood/infra/kms/commit/789 please review. It removes vendor group and adds condition binding for relay only.
lee: I'm drafting the log-based alert and a dashboard showing Decrypt counts per principal.
oncall: rewrap runbook note: if wrapping_key reassign fails, we should rollback by restoring previous KMS IAM policy and alerting. Keep known-good snapshot.
sec-bot: note: policy enforcement — add to infra-ci gate: scanning for `vault:v` strings in PRs, block merges that include them.
olga: good call. We currently have git-secrets but it's not catching vault ciphertexts. Add rule.
vendor-eng: deletion attestation posted to ticket: vendor-attest-545123.pdf (attached).
sam: status update: KMS IAM delta applied in staging, vendor group removed from policy. No decrypts observed in audit.
marta: proceeding with conditional IAM in prod now. Also creating log-based metric `kms-decrypt-unexpected` and alert policy to PagerDuty if >0 in 30m.
lee: vendor deletion confirmed. We should still rotate the specific wrapping key to be safe; rotation will be a primary key rotation (not destroy).
sec-bot: change: INCIDENT-2026-045 severity downgraded to low pending rotation completion.
oncall: starting rewrap in staging now (19:02). Will monitor Vault for errors.
oncall: staging rewrap completed successfully. No errors in Vault audit.
sam: running a fast repo-wide scan across mirrored vendor repos to ensure no other blobs: `for r in $(cat mirrors.txt); do git -C $r grep -n "vault:v[0-9]:" || true; done` — found one additional test fixture in vendor/test-fixtures, vendor will remove.
marta: prod rewrap scheduled for 19:30, rolling across vault nodes. Keep oncall on standby.
lee: asked infra to add org policy limiting `cloudkms.cryptoKeys.encrypterDecrypter` usage to service accounts with `serviceAccount:*-redwood-prod@*` format. That will prevent future external group bindings.
olga: vendor confirmed force-push and provided signed manifest. Thanks.
sec-bot: INCIDENT-2026-045 status changed to resolved.
marta: postmortem actions:
- add git hook / ci-scanner for `vault:v` patterns
- update onboarding guide: never commit KMS wrapped artifacts to vendor repos; use ephemeral artifacts or placeholders
- tighten KMS key IAM: condition-based bindings only
- add log-based metric + PagerDuty alert for KMS Decrypt from non-relay principals
- run org-wide scan for `vault:v` ciphertext in other public mirrors
lee: owners: marta (IAM + alert), sam (scans + backups), olga (CI rule + postmortem writeup), vendor-eng (repo hygiene + attestation).
olga: thanks all. I'll draft the postmortem and RFC for RBAC tightening.
vendor-eng: apologies again; we'll add precommit hooks in our onboard template.
sec-bot: postmortem link: https://confluence.redwood/security/postmortems/2026-045-kms-ciphertext-git-commit
